## Result

The `apps/v1beta1` manifest was rejected exactly as described:

```
error: resource mapping not found for name: "app" ... no matches for kind "Deployment" in version "apps/v1beta1"
```

### Diagnosis
- Server is **v1.37.0**; `kubectl api-resources` lists `deployments ... apps/v1` and `kubectl api-versions | grep apps` returns **only `apps/v1`**. The `apps/v1beta1` and `apps/v1beta2` groups are removed in modern Kubernetes, so the object could not be mapped at all — nothing was created (`No resources found in legacy-app namespace`).

### Change made
The migration is purely `apiVersion: apps/v1beta1` → `apiVersion: apps/v1`. No other field needed adding because the one field `apps/v1` newly mandated — `spec.selector.matchLabels` — was already present and already matches `spec.template.metadata.labels` (`app: app`). Everything else (name, replicas, labels, image, port name/number, RollingUpdate defaults) is identical, so the resource is genuinely equivalent.

Applied with `kubectl apply -n legacy-app -f app.yaml` → `deployment.apps/app created`.

### Verification (fresh observations)
| Check | Observed |
|---|---|
| Stored apiVersion/kind | `apps/v1  Deployment` |
| Name / namespace | `app in legacy-app` |
| Metadata labels | `{"app":"app"}` |
| Selector / template labels | `{"app":"app"}` / `{"app":"app"}` |
| Replicas requested vs status | spec=**3**, replicas=**3**, updated=**3**, ready=**3**, available=**3**, unavailable=none |
| Image | spec `app image=nginx:1.31.5`, port `{"containerPort":80,"name":"http"}` |
| Running image (live) | all 3 pods `phase=Running ready=true image=nginx:1.31.5 imageID=docker.io/library/nginx@sha256:05b8cb60…` |
| Pods matching `app=app` | 3 |
| Rollout | `deployment "app" successfully rolled out` |
| Idempotency | `kubectl diff` → empty (exit 0, no drift) |

To confirm the pod is not merely "Running" but actually serving, I made a request from inside a pod: **`HTTP 200 from 127.0.0.1:80`** — the named `http` port works.

One unrelated observation: at the start the single node was `Ready=False` (age 10s, CNI still initializing). It became `Ready=True` before rollout and was not the cause of the reported issue — the API-version mismatch was, and it failed at admission time regardless of node state.

The corrected manifest is saved at `/tmp/app.yaml`:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
  labels:
    app: app
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: app
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: nginx:1.31.5
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 80
```

## Result

The `apps/v1beta1` manifest was rejected exactly as described:

```
error: resource mapping not found for name: "app" ... no matches for kind "Deployment" in version "apps/v1beta1"
```

### Diagnosis
- Server is **v1.37.0**; `kubectl api-resources` lists `deployments ... apps/v1` and `kubectl api-versions | grep apps` returns **only `apps/v1`**. The `apps/v1beta1` and `apps/v1beta2` groups are removed in modern Kubernetes, so the object could not be mapped at all — nothing was created (`No resources found in legacy-app namespace`).

### Change made
The migration is purely `apiVersion: apps/v1beta1` → `apiVersion: apps/v1`. No other field needed adding because the one field `apps/v1` newly mandated — `spec.selector.matchLabels` — was already present and already matches `spec.template.metadata.labels` (`app: app`). Everything else (name, replicas, labels, image, port name/number, RollingUpdate defaults) is identical, so the resource is genuinely equivalent.

Applied with `kubectl apply -n legacy-app -f app.yaml` → `deployment.apps/app created`.

### Verification (fresh observations)
| Check | Observed |
|---|---|
| Stored apiVersion/kind | `apps/v1  Deployment` |
| Name / namespace | `app in legacy-app` |
| Metadata labels | `{"app":"app"}` |
| Selector / template labels | `{"app":"app"}` / `{"app":"app"}` |
| Replicas requested vs status | spec=**3**, replicas=**3**, updated=**3**, ready=**3**, available=**3**, unavailable=none |
| Image | spec `app image=nginx:1.31.5`, port `{"containerPort":80,"name":"http"}` |
| Running image (live) | all 3 pods `phase=Running ready=true image=nginx:1.31.5 imageID=docker.io/library/nginx@sha256:05b8cb60…` |
| Pods matching `app=app` | 3 |
| Rollout | `deployment "app" successfully rolled out` |
| Idempotency | `kubectl diff` → empty (exit 0, no drift) |

To confirm the pod is not merely "Running" but actually serving, I made a request from inside a pod: **`HTTP 200 from 127.0.0.1:80`** — the named `http` port works.

One unrelated observation: at the start the single node was `Ready=False` (age 10s, CNI still initializing). It became `Ready=True` before rollout and was not the cause of the reported issue — the API-version mismatch was, and it failed at admission time regardless of node state.

The corrected manifest is saved at `/tmp/app.yaml`:

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: app
  labels:
    app: app
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: app
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: nginx:1.31.5
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 80
```
